• Underline or mark every even number in the sequence first, then check just the very next number for each — this two-pass method avoids missing any qualifying pair.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the count (4) exceeds all specific numeric options (Two, Three, One), 'More than three' becomes the only fitting choice — always compute the exact count rather than guessing from the option wording.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs

are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT

belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. VR-WU.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: PL-QN, RN-SP, VR-WU, TP-UR.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert each letter to its alphabetical position (A=1...Z=26) and find the gap between the two letters of each half.

 

• PL-QN: P(16)→L(12), gap = −4; Q(17)→N(14), gap = −3. Pattern: (−4, −3).

 

• RN-SP: R(18)→N(14), gap = −4; S(19)→P(16), gap = −3. Pattern: (−4, −3). Matches.

 

• TP-UR: T(20)→P(16), gap = −4; U(21)→R(18), gap = −3. Pattern: (−4, −3). Matches.

 

• VR-WU: V(22)→R(18), gap = −4; W(23)→U(21), gap = −2. Pattern: (−4, −2). Does not match the (−4, −3) pattern of the rest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For letter-pair grouping questions, convert every letter to its numeric position and compute the gap within each mini-pair; the odd one out will show a gap value that breaks the otherwise consistent pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly rules out vowel/consonant-count logic, signalling that a purely numeric (alphabet-position) approach is the intended method here.

question:
Toshi starts from point A and drives 70 km towards east. He then takes a left turn, drives

45 km, turns left and drives 78 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 76 km. He takes a

final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards

which direction should he drive in order to reach point A again?

 

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 31 km to the north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Toshi: East 70 km → left turn, North 45 km → left turn, West 78 km → left turn, South 76 km → left turn (final), East 8 km, stops at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Each left turn rotates the direction 90° anticlockwise: East → North → West → South → East.

 

• Track net East–West displacement: +70 (east) − 78 (west) + 8 (east) = 70 − 78 + 8 = 0 (no net East-West displacement).

 

• Track net North–South displacement: +45 (north) − 76 (south) = 45 − 76 = −31 (i.e. 31 km south of start).

 

• So P is exactly 31 km south of A, with no east-west offset.

 

• To go from P back to A, Toshi must travel 31 km to the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track East-West and North-South movements as two separate running totals (treating east/north as positive, west/south as negative); the final position gives both the distance and direction to return, with the return direction always opposite to the sign of the net displacement.

 

NOTE

 

• With 4 consecutive left turns, the direction cycles back to the original (East) exactly after the 4th turn — useful for quickly checking that all five given distances have been assigned the correct direction (E, N, W, S, E).

question:
Ravindra starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards the east. He then takes a left turn,

drives 3 km, turns right and drives 4 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 8 km. He

takes a final right turn, drives 13 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance)

and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns

are 90 degrees turns only, unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5 km towards north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ravindra: East 9 km → left turn, North 3 km → right turn, East 4 km → right turn, South 8 km → right turn (final), West 13 km, stops at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Track direction changes: starts East. Left turn (East→North): North 3 km. Right turn (North→East): East 4 km. Right turn (East→South): South 8 km. Right turn (South→West): West 13 km.

 

• Net East-West displacement: +9 (east) + 4 (east) − 13 (west) = 9 + 4 − 13 = 0.

 

• Net North-South displacement: +3 (north) − 8 (south) = 3 − 8 = −5 (i.e., 5 km south of start).

 

• So P is exactly 5 km south of A, with zero east-west offset.

 

• To return from P to A, Ravindra must travel 5 km towards the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• As before, maintain two running totals — East-West and North-South — updating the current facing direction after every turn (left = 90° anticlockwise, right = 90° clockwise); the final net totals directly give the return distance and direction.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful to track the *current facing direction* correctly after each turn, since mixing left and right turns (unlike a series of all-left or all-right turns) changes the direction sequence in a less predictable, non-cyclic way.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', then what

will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

 

92 D 9 C 96 A 12 B 7 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 139.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 92 D 9 C 96 A 12 B 7 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 92 − 9 + 96 ÷ 12 × 7 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: division and multiplication first: 96 ÷ 12 = 8; 8 × 7 = 56.

 

• Now: 92 − 9 + 56.

 

• Left to right: 92 − 9 = 83; 83 + 56 = 139.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the entire expression by substituting the actual symbols in place of letters, then solve strictly by BODMAS — never perform operations in the letter-order given, always follow standard operator precedence after substitution.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to compute left to right ignoring precedence (e.g. doing 92−9 first, then +96, etc.) — always finish ÷ and × before + and −.

question:

• 'river child judge' → 'rr xi kt'.

question:
This question is based on the following words

COP, TIK, ANY, CAN, OWN

If in each of the words, each letter is changed to the next letter in the English

alphabetical order, how many words thus formed will have no vowel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Words: COP, TIK, ANY, CAN, OWN. Each letter is to be shifted to the next letter of the alphabet (C→D, O→P, etc.).

 

SOLUTION

 

• COP → D, P, Q = DPQ (no vowel among D, P, Q).

 

• TIK → U, J, L = UJL (contains U, a vowel).

 

• ANY → B, O, Z = BOZ (contains O, a vowel).

 

• CAN → D, B, O = DBO (contains O, a vowel).

 

• OWN → P, X, O = PXO (contains O, a vowel).

 

• Only DPQ (from COP) has no vowel at all — that's just one word.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Shift each letter of the word by +1 mentally (A→B, ..., Z→A) and immediately check if any of A, E, I, O, U appears in the shifted result — flag only the words with zero vowels.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember Z shifts back to A (wraparound) if any word contains Z — not the case here, but a common trap in such letter-shift questions.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the

given series to make it logically complete?

 

OSW 24, GKO 35, YCG 46, QUY 57, IMQ 68, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. AEI 79.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: OSW 24, GKO 35, YCG 46, QUY 57, IMQ 68, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number part: 24, 35, 46, 57, 68, ? — each increases by 11 (24+11=35, 35+11=46, ..., 68+11=79). So the missing number = 79.

 

• Letter part (checking each letter position, A=1...Z=26, mod 26): 1st letters O(15), G(7), Y(25), Q(17), I(9): each step is −8 (mod 26) — e.g., 15−8=7, 7−8=−1≡25, 25−8=17, 17−8=9, so next = 9−8=1 = A.

 

• 2nd letters S(19), K(11), C(3), U(21), M(13): also −8 (mod 26) each step — 19−8=11, 11−8=3, 3−8=−5≡21, 21−8=13, so next = 13−8=5 = E.

 

• 3rd letters W(23), O(15), G(7), Y(25), Q(17): also −8 (mod 26) each step — 23−8=15, 15−8=7, 7−8=−1≡25, 25−8=17, so next = 17−8=9 = I.

 

• Combined missing cluster = AEI 79.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a mixed letter-number cluster series into two independent series (numbers, and each letter position) and solve each separately — here the number part is a simple +11 AP, and each letter position follows a −8 (mod 26) cyclic pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Always use mod-26 wraparound for letter arithmetic; e.g., 7 − 8 = −1, which wraps around to 25 (Y), not a negative or invalid value.

question:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if '+' and '−'

are interchanged and 'x' and '÷' are interchanged?

 

15 + 17 ÷ 27 × 3 − 10 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. −128.

 

GIVEN

 

• '+' and '−' are interchanged; '×' and '÷' are interchanged. Equation: 15 + 17 ÷ 27 × 3 − 10 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• After interchanging, the equation becomes: 15 − 17 × 27 ÷ 3 + 10 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: multiplication/division first: 17 × 27 = 459; 459 ÷ 3 = 153.

 

• Now: 15 − 153 + 10.

 

• Left to right: 15 − 153 = −138; −138 + 10 = −128.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the whole expression first by swapping every '+'↔'−' and every '×'↔'÷' symbol throughout, then solve normally using BODMAS on the rewritten expression — don't try to swap results mentally mid-calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check that *every* occurrence of the swapped symbols has been changed — missing even one '+'/'−' or '×'/'÷' swap will silently give a wrong final answer.

question:
KOJM is related to QUPS in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the

same way, OSNQ is related to UYTW. To which of the following is GKFI related,

following the same logic?
solution_text:

GIVEN

 

• KOJM → QUPS; OSNQ → UYTW. Find the term related to GKFI by the same logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter-by-letter shift from KOJM to QUPS (A=1...Z=26): K(11)→Q(17): +6; O(15)→U(21): +6; J(10)→P(16): +6; M(13)→S(19): +6. So each letter shifts by +6.

 

• Verify with OSNQ → UYTW: O(15)→U(21): +6; S(19)→Y(25): +6; N(14)→T(20): +6; Q(17)→W(23): +6. Confirmed, consistent +6 shift.

 

• Apply the same +6 shift to GKFI: G(7)+6=13=M; K(11)+6=17=Q; F(6)+6=12=L; I(9)+6=15=O.

 

• Result: MQLO.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'word is related to word' letter-coding questions, check the shift on just the first letter pair; if it holds consistently for all letters in a second worked example, apply that same fixed shift to the new word.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch for wraparound past Z when adding a shift value (not needed here since no letter exceeds 26 after +6), and always double check against the second given example, not just the first.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

 

Statements:

All hammers are screwdrivers.

Some screwdrivers are wrenches.

No wrenches are pliers.

 

Conclusions:

(I): Some pliers are screwdrivers.

(II): Some wrenches are hammers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) is true.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All hammers are screwdrivers. Some screwdrivers are wrenches. No wrenches are pliers.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Conclusion I ('Some pliers are screwdrivers'): We know 'Some screwdrivers are wrenches' and 'No wrenches are pliers'; a particular (some) statement combined with a negative (no) statement about a *different* class generally yields no definite conclusion about pliers and screwdrivers — screwdriver-wrench overlap doesn't tell us anything about screwdriver-pliers overlap, so Conclusion I does not necessarily follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('Some wrenches are hammers'): 'All hammers are screwdrivers' only places hammers *inside* screwdrivers; 'Some screwdrivers are wrenches' doesn't guarantee that the specific screwdrivers overlapping with wrenches are the same ones that are hammers — so this link cannot be established with certainty either.

 

• Since neither conclusion can be validly and definitely drawn from the given statements using standard syllogism rules, the answer is that neither follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Two 'Some' (particular) type statements, or a 'Some' combined with a 'No' about unrelated end-classes, almost never yield a definite conclusion — be suspicious of any conclusion that tries to bridge classes only loosely connected via a 'some' statement.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw a quick Venn diagram for such 3-statement syllogisms — it makes it visually obvious when an overlap is only 'possible' rather than 'certain', which is exactly the case for both conclusions here.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of

the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down

the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding

to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and

3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(18, 324, 1)

(7, 71, 23)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (22, 505, 22).

 

GIVEN

 

• Sets (18, 324, 1) and (7, 71, 23) follow a hidden pattern relating the first (a), second (b) and third (c) numbers.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the relation b = a² + c − 1 on the first set: 18² + 1 − 1 = 324 + 0 = 324 ✔ (matches).

 

• Test the same relation on the second set: 7² + 23 − 1 = 49 + 22 = 71 ✔ (matches).

 

• So the rule is confirmed: b = a² + c − 1.

 

• Check option (22, 505, 22): 22² + 22 − 1 = 484 + 21 = 505 ✔ (matches exactly).

 

• Check the other options: (22,501,13): 484+13−1=496≠501; (44,1955,15): 44²+15−1=1936+14=1950≠1955; (1,30,25): 1+25−1=25≠30 — none of these satisfy the rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two given number-triplets share a pattern, always test relations involving a square or product of the first number combined with the third (since simple sums rarely fit both sets) — squaring the first term is a common trick in such 'whole number operation' series.

 

NOTE

 

• Strictly avoid digit-breaking (as the question itself warns) — always treat each number as one indivisible whole quantity while forming or testing the relation.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are

alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to

that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. PTN.

 

GIVEN

 

• Clusters: EIB, SWP, PTN, VZS.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert each letter to its alphabet position (A=1...Z=26) and find the gap between consecutive letters within each cluster.

 

• EIB: E(5)→I(9): +4; I(9)→B(2): −7 (mod 26, since 9−7=2 directly without wraparound issue, but checked as a consistent −7 step... actually 9 to 2 is a drop of 7). Pattern: (+4, −7).

 

• SWP: S(19)→W(23): +4; W(23)→P(16): −7. Pattern: (+4, −7). Matches EIB.

 

• VZS: V(22)→Z(26): +4; Z(26)→S(19): −7. Pattern: (+4, −7). Matches.

 

• PTN: P(16)→T(20): +4; T(20)→N(14): −6 (not −7). Pattern: (+4, −6). Does not match the rest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to numbers and compute the two internal gaps of each 3-letter cluster; three clusters sharing an identical gap-pattern form the group, and the one with a different second gap is the odd one out.

 

NOTE

 

• Small differences (like −6 instead of −7) are easy to miss without carefully recomputing each letter's numeric position — always double-check the arithmetic rather than estimating alphabet positions visually.

question:
In a certain code language,

'A + B' means 'A is the son of B'

'A – B' means 'A is the brother of B'

'A × B' means 'A is the wife of B'

'A ÷ B' means 'A is the father of B'

Based on the above, how is D related to J if 'D × F + G ÷ H – J'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Brother's wife.

 

GIVEN

 

• Codes: '+' = son of, '−' = brother of, '×' = wife of, '÷' = father of. Expression: D × F + G ÷ H − J.

 

SOLUTION

 

• D × F: D is the wife of F.

 

• F + G: F is the son of G.

 

• G ÷ H: G is the father of H. (So H's father is G, and F is also G's son — meaning F and H are siblings, children of G.)

 

• H − J: H is the brother of J. (So H and J are also siblings, sharing the same father G — meaning J is also G's child.)

 

• Since F, H and J are all children of G (siblings), and D is the wife of F, D is married into the family through F, who is J's brother.

 

• Therefore, D is J's brother's wife.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode such family-relation-coded chains one symbol at a time from left to right, building a small family tree/diagram as you go — trying to reason about all relations at once leads to mistakes.

 

NOTE

 

• Always track gender implied by relation words used ('son', 'father', 'brother' imply male; 'wife' implies the person is female and married in) to correctly phrase the final relation, like 'brother's wife' rather than a same-gender relation term.

question:
A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting in a straight line facing north. Only three people sit

between W and Y. A sits to the immediate left of Y. No one sits to the right of B. Only

two people sit between B and A. X sits to the immediate right of D. How many people sit

between C and X?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A,B,C,D,W,X,Y) in a straight line facing north. 3 people between W and Y; A immediately left of Y; no one right of B; 2 people between B and A; X immediately right of D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number positions 1 (extreme left) to 7 (extreme right). 'No one sits to the right of B' ⇒ B = position 7.

 

• 'Only two people sit between B and A' ⇒ A is 3 seats away from B ⇒ A = 7 − 3 = 4.

 

• 'A sits to the immediate left of Y' ⇒ Y = A + 1 = 5.

 

• 'Only three people sit between W and Y' ⇒ W is 4 seats away from Y(5) ⇒ W = 5 − 4 = 1 (5+4=9 is out of range).

 

• Remaining positions {2, 3, 6} go to C, D, X, with X immediately right of D (X = D + 1). Testing: D=2, X=3 works (both in the remaining set); D=6, X=7 is taken by B. So D = 2, X = 3, leaving C = 6.

 

• Final order: W(1), D(2), X(3), A(4), Y(5), C(6), B(7).

 

• People between C(6) and X(3): positions 4, 5 = A, Y = two people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Anchor the row using the strongest clue first ('no one to the right of B' fixes B absolutely at an end), then resolve each subsequent clue as a fixed offset from already-placed people.

 

NOTE

 

• When a clue like 'X is immediate right of D' allows multiple placements among the remaining empty seats, test each candidate against the already-filled seats to eliminate invalid options quickly.

question:
In a row of 41 people facing north, Mohan is 10th from the left end. If Rahul sits 9th to

the right of Mohan, what is Rahul's position from the right end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 23rd.

 

GIVEN

 

• Row of 41 people; Mohan is 10th from the left end; Rahul sits 9th to the right of Mohan.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Mohan's position from the left = 10.

 

• Rahul is 9th to the right of Mohan, so Rahul's position from the left = 10 + 9 = 19.

 

• Position from the right end = (Total people − Position from left) + 1 = (41 − 19) + 1 = 22 + 1 = 23rd.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the standard formula: Position from right = (Total + 1) − Position from left. Here: (41 + 1) − 19 = 42 − 19 = 23.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute the absolute position from one end first (here, from the left, since Mohan's and Rahul's positions are naturally given relative to the left), then convert to the other end using the total count.

question:
Refer to the given number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be

done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

 

(Left) 8 2 6 4 7 3 5 1 9 8 3 7 2 6 5 9 1 4 8 7 2 6 9 3 5 8 (Right).

 

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd

digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:

GIVEN

SOLUTION

• Position 12 (value 7): preceded by position 11 (value 3, odd) ✔, followed by position 13 (value 2, even) ✔. Counts.

• Position 25 (value 5): preceded by position 24 (value 3, odd) ✔, followed by position 26 (value 8, even) ✔. Counts.

 

• Checking all other odd digits in the sequence confirms no further matches; total = 4 (Four).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Scan the sequence once, marking every 'odd-odd' consecutive pair; then, for each such pair, simply check whether the digit right after the second odd digit is even — this two-step filtering is faster than checking every digit individually from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful with overlapping runs of odd numbers (e.g., three odd digits in a row) — only the odd digit whose immediate follower is even qualifies, not every odd digit in the run.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

question:

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

 

(Left) 783 791 531 563 594 (Right)

(Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.

 

What will be the resultant if the second digit of the highest number is added to the

second digit of the lowest number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 12.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 783, 791, 531, 563, 594.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The highest number among these is 791; its second digit is 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

NOTE

question:
In the following triad, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a

certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

 

CLUB - LCUB - CUBL

SEAT - ESAT - SATE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. PALE - APLE - PLEA.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern: CLUB → LCUB → CUBL; SEAT → ESAT → SATE.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): swap the first two letters. CLUB (C,L,U,B) → swap C,L → LCUB ✔. SEAT (S,E,A,T) → swap S,E → ESAT ✔.

 

• Step 2 (word2 → word3): move the first letter to the end (left-rotate by one). LCUB → drop L from front, add at end → CUBL ✔. ESAT → drop E, add at end → SATE ✔.

 

• Apply this two-step logic to each option's first word and check: PALE (P,A,L,E) → swap first two (P,A) → APLE ✔ matches option's word2; then rotate APLE (drop A, add at end) → PLEA ✔ matches option's word3.

 

• The remaining options (TWIN, GROW, HOME) fail at either the swap step or the rotation step when checked the same way.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Break such 'triad' pattern questions into two separate, simple operations (here: swap-first-two, then rotate-first-to-last) and verify each option against both steps individually rather than trying to spot the whole pattern at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Always test both transformations (word1→word2 AND word2→word3) for a candidate option — a word might satisfy the first step by coincidence but fail the second.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for 'x', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '-', what will be

come in place of question mark '?' in the following equation?

 

41 C 12 A 6 D 5 B 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 33.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 41 C 12 A 6 D 5 B 2 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 41 + 12 ÷ 6 − 5 × 2 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: division and multiplication first: 12 ÷ 6 = 2; 5 × 2 = 10.

 

• Now: 41 + 2 − 10.

 

• Left to right: 41 + 2 = 43; 43 − 10 = 33.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Substitute all letter-codes with their actual operators in one pass first, then apply BODMAS strictly (÷/× before +/−) rather than solving operation-by-operation in the order the letters appear.

 

NOTE

 

• Re-check the letter-to-symbol mapping carefully each time, since different questions in the same test may assign different letters to the same operators (a common source of careless errors).

question:
Seven boxes, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are kept one over the other but not necessarily in

the same order. Only C is kept above B. Only E is kept between B and F. Only G is kept

below A. How many boxes are kept below F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes (A–G) stacked in a pile. Only C is above B. Only E is between B and F. Only G is below A.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number positions 1 (bottom) to 7 (top).

 

• 'Only G is kept below A' ⇒ exactly one box (G) is below A ⇒ A is at position 2, and G is at position 1 (bottom).

 

• 'Only C is kept above B' ⇒ exactly one box (C) is above B ⇒ B is at position 6, and C is at position 7 (top).

 

• 'Only E is kept between B and F' ⇒ exactly one box (E) lies between B(6) and F. Testing F = 6 − 2 = 4 (with E at position 5 in between) fits, since F = 8 (the other direction) is out of range.

 

• Remaining position 3 goes to the only box left, D.

 

• Final order (bottom to top): G(1), A(2), D(3), F(4), E(5), B(6), C(7).

 

• Boxes below F(4): positions 1, 2, 3 = G, A, D = 3 boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Resolve 'only X is below/above Y' clues first — they fix absolute positions immediately (since 'only one box below/above' pins a box to the 2nd position from that end), then work inward using the remaining relative clues.

 

NOTE

 

• In stacking/pile puzzles, always explicitly decide whether position '1' means bottom or top before starting, and stay consistent throughout to avoid direction-flip errors.

• State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest public sector bank, launched 'Next LEAP' in 2025 as its largest-ever staff engagement initiative, aimed at empowering its vast workforce through leadership development, employee well-being, and skill-enhancement programmes. (SBI 'नेक्स्ट लीप' — कर्मचारी सशक्तिकरण पहल, 2025)

 

• The initiative underscores SBI's continued focus on human capital development as it navigates rapid digital transformation in the banking sector, aiming to keep its massive employee base future-ready.

 

• Given SBI's scale — the bank has the largest branch network and employee strength among Indian banks — 'Next LEAP' was described as one of the largest workforce engagement programmes undertaken by any Indian bank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• State Bank of India (SBI) traces its origins to the Bank of Calcutta (1806), later becoming the Imperial Bank of India, and was renamed State Bank of India in 1955.

 

• SBI's current Chairman and other top public sector bank leadership are appointed via the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB)'s recommendations.

 

• Other major PSU banks — Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and Indian Bank — also run their own internal HR and training initiatives, but 'Next LEAP' specifically refers to SBI's programme.

question: The inaugural Everest Climbers' Summit, focused on climate, held in 2025, took place in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathmandu, Nepal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The inaugural Everest Climbers' Summit, focused on climate change and its impact on the Himalayas, was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in 2025 — a fitting venue given Nepal's status as home to Mount Everest. (एवरेस्ट क्लाइम्बर्स समिट — काठमांडू, नेपाल)

 

• The summit brought together mountaineers, climate scientists, and policymakers to discuss the effects of glacial melting, black carbon pollution, and rising temperatures on the world's highest peaks and the communities dependent on Himalayan glacial water systems.

 

• Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), straddling the Nepal-China (Tibet) border, is the world's highest peak and a focal point for climate research due to visible glacial retreat in recent decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal and the traditional base for expeditions to Mount Everest and other Himalayan peaks.

 

• The Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region, sometimes called the 'Third Pole', holds the largest volume of ice outside the polar regions and is a critical freshwater source for South Asia.

 

• International bodies like ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development), headquartered in Kathmandu, regularly publish reports on Himalayan climate change impacts.

 

NOTE

 

• Lhasa, Tibet (Option A): The Tibetan approach base for Everest's north side, but not the venue for this particular summit.

 

• Dhaka, Bangladesh (Option C) and Dharamsala, India (Option D): Neither city hosted this inaugural Everest-focused climate summit, which was held in Kathmandu.

question: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, is also known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is UMEED Act.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, is officially also referred to as the UMEED Act, an acronym standing for 'Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development'. (वक्फ संशोधन अधिनियम 2025 — 'उम्मीद' अधिनियम)

 

• The Act brought significant changes to the governance of Waqf properties in India, including reforms to Waqf Boards' composition, registration and verification processes, and mechanisms for dispute resolution over Waqf land.

 

• It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in 2025 after extensive debate, amending the earlier Waqf Act, 1995, and drew both support and opposition regarding its impact on the management of religious endowment properties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Waqf refers to a permanent dedication of movable or immovable property by a Muslim for purposes recognised as pious, religious, or charitable under Islamic law.

 

• The Central Waqf Council and State Waqf Boards are the key bodies responsible for administering Waqf properties across India.

 

• The amendment process involved a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the bill before its passage, reflecting the significant stakeholder consultation involved.

 

NOTE

 

• TAHIB Act, SAHIB Act and FARID Act (Options A, B, C): These are fabricated/incorrect names — the official short/popular name given to this legislation is the UMEED Act, not these.

question:
Which team did the Indian women's team defeat to emerge as champions in the

inaugural Kho Kho World Cup on 19 January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian women's Kho Kho team defeated Nepal in the final to become champions of the inaugural Kho Kho World Cup, held on 19 January 2025 in New Delhi. (खो-खो विश्व कप 2025 — भारत बनाम नेपाल फाइनल)

 

• Both the Indian men's and women's teams won their respective finals at this first-ever Kho Kho World Cup, with the men's team also defeating Nepal in their final, making it a memorable clean sweep for India as host nation.

 

• The tournament, organised by the Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI) under the International Kho Kho Federation, marked a landmark moment for the indigenous Indian sport's global outreach, featuring both men's and women's categories with multiple participating nations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kho Kho is a traditional Indian tag sport, one of the oldest team sports in South Asia, alongside Kabaddi.

 

• India also hosted and won titles in international Kabaddi World Cups, reflecting the country's dominance in indigenous team sports.

 

• The Ultimate Kho Kho (UKK) league, launched in 2022, has helped popularise a faster, more spectator-friendly version of the sport domestically in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option B), Bangladesh (Option C) and China (Option D): None of these teams were India's opponent in the women's final of the 2025 Kho Kho World Cup — Nepal was the finalist India defeated.

question: Who chaired the 10th Governing Council Meeting of the NITI Aayog on 24 May 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 10th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog, held on 24 May 2025, was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog. (नीति आयोग की 10वीं गवर्निंग काउंसिल बैठक — प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी)

 

• The Governing Council of NITI Aayog comprises all State Chief Ministers, Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, and select Union Ministers, serving as the apex body for cooperative federalism-based policy discussions between the Centre and states.

 

• Such meetings typically focus on key national development priorities, including the roadmap for 'Viksit Bharat @2047', sectoral reforms, and state-specific development challenges.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was constituted on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission, embodying the concept of 'cooperative and competitive federalism'.

 

• The Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog (currently a senior economist/policy expert appointed by the PM) manages day-to-day functioning, while the CEO is a senior civil servant.

 

• The Governing Council is NITI Aayog's highest decision-making body, distinct from smaller sub-groups and task forces formed for specific policy areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Amit Shah (Option A): Union Home Minister, an important cabinet member but not the Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

 

• JP Nadda (Option C): President of the BJP and Union Health Minister, not the NITI Aayog Chairperson.

 

• Manohar Lal Khattar (Option D): Union Minister and former Haryana Chief Minister, not the Chairperson of this meeting.

question: Which of the following institutions won the Bakshi Cup in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Naval Academy (INA).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Naval Academy (INA), located at Ezhimala, Kerala, won the prestigious Bakshi Cup in 2025. (बख्शी कप 2025 — भारतीय नौसेना अकादमी)

 

• The Bakshi Cup is awarded as part of inter-service/inter-academy competitions among India's premier defence training institutions, recognising excellence in training, discipline, and overall performance among cadets.

 

• The Indian Naval Academy trains cadets for commissioning into the Indian Navy, offering various entry schemes including the Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) programme for cadets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Defence Academy (NDA), located at Khadakwasla, Pune, is the first tri-services academy in the world, training cadets for the Army, Navy and Air Force together before they proceed to their respective service-specific academies.

 

• The Indian Military Academy (IMA), located in Dehradun, trains officers for the Indian Army, while the Air Force Academy (AFA), located near Hyderabad (Dundigal), trains officers for the Indian Air Force.

 

• Such inter-academy trophies and cups (like the Bakshi Cup) foster healthy competition and camaraderie among India's various defence training institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Military Academy (Option B), Air Force Academy (Option C) and National Defence Academy (Option D): All are premier Indian defence training institutions, but the Bakshi Cup for 2025 was won specifically by the Indian Naval Academy.

question:
In May 2025, the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) recommended Asheesh

Pandey as the new Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of which

bank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Bank of India.

• In May 2025, the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) recommended Asheesh Pandey for appointment as the new Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Union Bank of India. (एशीष पांडेय — यूनियन बैंक ऑफ इंडिया एमडी एवं सीईओ)

 

• Asheesh Pandey previously served as an Executive Director at a public sector bank before being recommended for this top leadership position, as part of the routine process of senior public sector bank leadership appointments.

 

• The FSIB is the body responsible for recommending appointments to the Boards of Public Sector Banks (PSBs), financial institutions, and insurance companies in India, having replaced the earlier Banks Board Bureau (BBB).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Union Bank of India, headquartered in Mumbai, is one of India's leading public sector banks, formed after the merger of Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank into it in 2020.

 

• The FSIB (Financial Services Institutions Bureau) was constituted in 2022, expanding the mandate of the earlier Banks Board Bureau to also cover insurance companies and financial institutions.

 

• MD & CEO appointments to public sector banks in India are formally made by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), based on FSIB's recommendations.

 

NOTE

 

• Canara Bank, Central Bank of India and State Bank of India (Options B, C, D): All major public sector banks with their own separately appointed MD/CEO or Chairman leadership; Asheesh Pandey's May 2025 recommendation was specifically for Union Bank of India.
